podcast-dannyjones-8jksrbKGGSM:
Travis Kitchens returns to Danny Jones's podcast with a claim pitched at full volume. Billionaires, he says, are secretly funding a psychedelic holy war. In his account they bankroll the spread of mind-altering drugs as a spiritual and political project. Kitchens connects foundations, research money, and the psychedelic revival into one design.

Jones works through the money trail with him, name by name. The revival itself is real and well funded, and readers can verify its donors; the holy war framing is Kitchens's interpretation of that money's purpose. The episode keeps the two separate in presentation even when the guest merges them. For listeners tracking how psychedelics moved from counterculture to boardrooms, the conversation offers a suspicious, detailed, and arguable map of who paid for the trip.
podcast-joerogan-cdP3L73yySM:
Commentator Hotep Jesus sits with Rogan for episode 1318 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Known for blunt online broadcasts, he brings an unfiltered take on race, culture, and the internet's wars. The talk is fiery by design, and Rogan lets it run hot.

The two argue and joke their way across the subjects that built his following, from media narratives to personal responsibility. Rogan pushes back where the claims stretch and laughs where they land. The episode preserves a provocative voice at full volume, the kind of guest booking that made the young show a free-speech landmark for its fans.
podcast-joerogan-p6LJXPOv4SM:
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. sits with Joe Rogan for episode 1999, recorded while Kennedy was running for president. Kennedy, an environmental lawyer from the famous political family, had broken with the Democratic Party. The long talk gave his campaign one of its biggest platforms.

Kennedy lays out his views on vaccines, public health agencies, and corporate power over government. He also talks about the environment and the legacy of his father and uncle, both killed in the 1960s. Rogan lets him speak at length with few interruptions. The episode became a key moment in Kennedy's run and in Rogan's political reach.
